title: AWS Cloud-Native Architecture, Amazon EKS & Karpenter
summary: Architect production Amazon EKS clusters, IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA / Pod Identity), AWS VPC CNI, ALB Controller, and Karpenter node provisioning.
learningObjectives: Provision and inspect Amazon EKS control planes via the AWS CLI.
Configure IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) using OIDC federated ServiceAccount annotations.
Define Karpenter NodePool resources for rapid, right-sized EC2 Spot/On-Demand provisioning.

curriculumModules.title: Amazon EKS Control Plane, VPC CNI & IRSA Workload Identity
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Amazon EKS runs a multi-AZ managed control plane. IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) uses OIDC token projection so Pods assume scoped AWS IAM Roles without static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID secrets.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Annotate Kubernetes ServiceAccounts with `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` and scope the IAM Trust Policy to the exact namespace and ServiceAccount name.

curriculumModules.title: Groupless Node Autoscaling with Karpenter
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Unlike legacy Cluster Autoscaler tied to static EC2 Auto Scaling Groups, Karpenter watches unschedulable pods directly and launches optimal EC2 instances in seconds.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Define a Karpenter `NodePool` with Spot + On-Demand consolidation enabled (`consolidationPolicy: WhenEmptyOrUnderutilized`).

labs.title: Amazon EKS Cluster Inspection & IRSA IAM Role Binding
labs.scenario: Verify the `kubelabs-eks-prod` cluster via AWS CLI and configure a Kubernetes `ServiceAccount` (`s3-uploader-sa`) in `production` annotated with IAM Role `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/eks-s3-uploader`.
labs.productionContext: IRSA eliminates long-lived AWS IAM access keys from Kubernetes Secrets, using short-lived OIDC web identity tokens instead.
objectives: Inspect the EKS cluster using `aws eks describe-cluster --name kubelabs-eks-prod`
Create ServiceAccount `s3-uploader-sa` in `production` and annotate it with `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/eks-s3-uploader`
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: s3-uploader-sa
  namespace: production
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/eks-s3-uploader

steps.title: Create & Annotate IRSA ServiceAccount
steps.instruction: Create `s3-uploader-sa` in `production` and annotate it with `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/eks-s3-uploader`.

validationRules.description: Amazon EKS cluster kubelabs-eks-prod verified ACTIVE
validationRules.name: kubelabs-eks-prod

validationRules.description: ServiceAccount production/s3-uploader-sa has IRSA role-arn annotation
validationRules.name: s3-uploader-sa
validationRules.remediation: Create s3-uploader-sa and run `kubectl annotate serviceaccount s3-uploader-sa eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/eks-s3-uploader -n production`.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Check `kubectl describe sa s3-uploader-sa -n production` to confirm the `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` annotation.

labs.title: Configuring a Karpenter Elastic NodePool
labs.scenario: Provision a Karpenter `NodePool` named `spot-compute-pool` to enable rapid Spot/On-Demand EC2 compute consolidation.
labs.productionContext: Karpenter NodePools dynamically select instance families and availability zones to minimize compute waste.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: spot-compute-pool
  labels:
    karpenter.sh/capacity-type: spot
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Run `kubectl get nodepool spot-compute-pool -o json` to verify the label.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does Amazon EKS IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) grant AWS API permissions to a Pod without static IAM credentials?
options: By mounting the EC2 worker node's root SSH key into every container
By projecting a signed OIDC service account token into the Pod and exchanging it via AWS STS `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`
By storing AWS root account credentials in a ConfigMap
By disabling IAM validation in VPC endpoints
assessmentQuestions.explanation: IRSA uses Kubernetes projected service account tokens validated against the cluster's OIDC provider via AWS STS `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does AWS VPC CNI assign IP addresses to Pods on Amazon EKS?
options: It allocates secondary private IPv4/IPv6 addresses directly from the AWS VPC subnet via Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs)
Every Pod shares 127.0.0.1 across all nodes
It requires public IPv4 addresses for every internal pod
assessmentQuestions.explanation: AWS VPC CNI attaches ENIs and secondary VPC IP addresses to worker nodes so Pods have first-class routable VPC IPs.
